name: Tuff ASR zh (q5_1)
description: Size-optimized sibling of tuff-asr-zh 0.1.0: the same whisper-base weights, quantized to q5_1. The unquantized bundle is 148 MB to download, which is a real first-run cost, so a 60 MB bundle that transcribes the same audio about as well is the better trade for a desktop app. Measurements on two utterances found no quality difference in either direction, which is too little evidence to call parity: this release is installable but is not the catalog default. No training was performed; this is a quantization, not a new model. See docs/versions/tuff-asr-zh-0.2.0.md.

benchmark.dataset: 2 synthetic Mandarin utterances via macOS say -v Tingting (3.44 s and 2.9 s), 5 repetitions per configuration
benchmark.notes: NOT a benchmark — 2 utterances cannot establish parity, and this is recorded so the claim is not mistaken for one. Decoded with the runtime's own flags (whisper-cli -oj, timestamps enabled) because that flag changes the transcript, not just the output format; plain '-nt' runs produce different text from the same weights. All 5 repetitions of each configuration were byte-identical. Utterance 1 (今天天气很好我们去公园散步吧): 0.1.0 -> ...去公元散步吧 (公元 wrong); 0.2.0 -> 今天天起很好我们去公园散步吧 (起 wrong, 公园 right). One distinct error each. Utterance 2 (明天下午三点开会记得带上项目文档): both -> 明天下午三点开会计的戴上项目文档, differing only in closing punctuation. Therefore no quality difference is established in either direction, and the dominant error source is whisper base itself, not the quantization.
